clips.title: Renovate For Dependency Management | Installation and Usage | Dependabot Vs Renovate | Advantages |
clips.why: A quick tour of how Renovate's update PRs look and how its configuration shapes them, so the renovate.json5 in this lesson reads like something familiar.
look: How update PRs appear, and how much a person has to read to approve one.
Which settings change how many PRs you get, and how often.
clips.after: Our configuration turns those settings toward quiet: one group per team, once a month, nothing younger than a week, majors alone.

clips.title: Git Bisect - Your History's Saviour
clips.why: git bisect finds the change that broke something by testing step by step. Trying each bump alone is the same idea, with packages instead of commits.
look: The question bisect answers is "which change broke it?", and it answers it with tests, not guesses.
Each step tests one candidate against a known good starting point.
clips.after: The upgrade fixer's first step uses no model: each bump alone on the base commit, and the red ones are the culprits.

practice.q: Finish the rule for where every bump is tried in step 1.
practice.before: Each bump is applied alone on the
practice.after: commit, the main commit the Renovate branch started from.
practice.hint: Four letters; the starting point of the branch.
practice.why: Starting every try from the same commit means a red result belongs to that one bump.

practice.q: Put the upgrade fixer's work in order.
items: A Renovate group PR fails frontend CI and wakes the fixer
Each bump is tried alone on the base commit
One fix session runs for the one package that broke the build
All fixes are checked together on the Renovate branch
The fix commits are pushed to the Renovate branch, and a person reviews the PR
practice.why: Find the culprit first, fix it small, and prove the whole group together before anything is pushed.

practice.q: A Renovate group bumps protobuf and two other Python packages, and cloud CI is red because of protobuf. What does the backend upgrade fixer do with protobuf?

options.text: Fixes our code for the new protobuf like any other package
options.why: protobuf and the gRPC packages are the contract between cloud and client. Changing them is a decision for people.

options.text: Hands it to the backend guild with the failure, and may still fix the other packages
options.why: The charter lists these packages as hand-offs, so the routine never touches them.

options.text: Removes protobuf from the group so the PR turns green
options.why: Editing the group to hide a failure is the upgrade version of a false heal.

practice.q: Why does every major version get its own Renovate PR instead of joining the team's group?

options.text: Because majors are the updates most likely to need real code changes, so a fixer and a reviewer can take each one alone
options.why: A major in a group would turn the whole monthly PR red and mix its work with nine easy updates.
It can. We switch grouping off for majors on purpose.

options.text: Because majors are proposed sooner than the 7-day minimum
options.why: The 7-day minimum release age applies to majors too.
